source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Compartment syndrome generally resolving on its own over time without ever requiring any active emergency surgical or medical intervention from the treating team at the bedside","B":"Symptoms generally developing right away with fairly little further progression at all occurring over the following several hours after the client's initial injury","C":"Compartment syndrome is a limb-threatening emergency in which increased pressure within a muscle compartment compromises blood flow, requiring rapid recognition and intervention to prevent permanent damage","D":"This particular complication lacking any established clinical approach for how nurses should go about assessing for its early warning signs and overall presence during routine checks"}}
source_row.rationale: Compartment syndrome is a limb-threatening emergency in which increased pressure within a closed muscle compartment compromises blood flow to nerves and muscle, requiring rapid recognition (often progressing over hours) and intervention, such as emergency fasciotomy, to prevent permanent tissue damage or limb loss.
source_row.source_detail: Critical Nature of Early Compartment Syndrome Detection
